seeds.title: Grant application quality / win-rate support for UK SMEs
seeds.observation: The GrantScout adversarial pass observed that the value in UK grant funding may lie in application quality and win rate rather than discovery - discovery is free from GOV.UK Find a grant, while applications are long, competitive and often rejected.
seeds.why_materially_different: A win-rate/application-quality proposition serves a different job (prepare a winning bid) from a £15-£29/mo discovery digest, likely with a different pricing model (contingency or per-application) and a different buyer. It must be researched from scratch and may fail the same margin, distribution and wedge filters.

seeds.title: Agentic-checkout readiness for off-platform merchants
seeds.observation: The AgentReady kill found that the major commerce platforms bundle agentic checkout and AI-channel distribution into their standard offering (Shopify Agentic Storefronts with no apps or fees beyond standard processing; Shopify/Stripe/Google/WooCommerce/BigCommerce/Salesforce all shipping ACP/UCP support). Merchants on off-platform or custom storefronts do not get a first-party agentic channel, so a narrow integration-and-assurance service for custom stacks might persist where the platform bundles do not reach.
seeds.why_materially_different: It serves a different buyer (custom/headless merchants and the small agencies that build for them, not the general independent merchant population covered for free by the platforms) with a different mechanism (integration/assurance on top of ACP/UCP endpoints and product feeds, not a productised readiness tool). Its competitive position is defined by what the platform bundles do not reach, which the parent's commodity kill did not test. It must be researched from scratch and may fail the same wedge and margin filters.

seeds.title: UK EPR packaging tooling for small producers
seeds.observation: The PackProof kill found the EU PPWR compliance-software space crowded (PPWR Copilot, PPWRify, PPWR Connect, Trace One and others). UK EPR for packaging is a distinct regime from EU PPWR: large UK producers register annually, report every six months, buy PRNs/PERNs and pay the PackUK waste disposal fee, while small producers register and report by 1 April with data-retention duties. The EU-focused PPWR vendors may not serve this UK-only workflow.
seeds.why_materially_different: It addresses a different regulation and buyer (UK EPR obligations for UK producers, not EU PPWR duties for exporters into the EU) with a different job (recurring registration, reporting and PRN/PERN obligations rather than packaging dossiers and Declarations of Conformity), against a different competitive set (UK EPR compliance schemes and obligated-producer reporting tools). It must be researched from scratch and may fail the same wedge and regulation filters.

seeds.title: Written-estimate to itemised-bill bridge for independent vet practices
seeds.observation: The CMA draft Order requires written estimates for pathways likely to cost GBP500 or more and itemised bills, while independents on legacy PMS or dated websites may lack a fee-transparency workflow at the point of treatment; incumbents market bundled compliance suites rather than a bridge to existing systems.
seeds.why_materially_different: A narrow workflow/integration wedge tied to fee capture during treatment, not a price-list or compliance-suite product.

seeds.title: PRS listing pre-check and landlord registration-number chase
seeds.observation: Agents may not market a relevant rental property without active Landlord and Property Registration Numbers, and at the draft-regulations stage there was no known bulk-upload or API route for agents.
seeds.why_materially_different: A validation/API wedge aimed at portals and CRM vendors rather than another agent-facing compliance suite.

seeds.title: Ongoing AML monitoring of corporate property ownership for small conveyancers
seeds.observation: HM Land Registry is adding property identifiers to Price Paid Data (live 28 August 2026) and plans the same for UK and Overseas Companies data in FY2026-27, which with Economic Crime Act obligations could support ongoing ownership-change monitoring.
seeds.why_materially_different: A monitoring/ongoing-compliance service for smaller conveyancers, not a commodity data index.

seeds.title: UK/EU green-list waste shipment documentation bridge
seeds.observation: The WasteTrack kill found the domestic receiver-side digital waste tracking market saturated, but noted that the EU's Digital Waste Shipment System (DIWASS) became the mandatory route for transboundary waste shipments from 21 May 2026 with reported adoption only ~18.1% of ~137,000 eligible operators, while UK green-list (Article 18) tracking was deferred to a future UK DWT phase and waste carrier/broker/dealer registration becomes permit-based from 22 July 2027.
seeds.why_materially_different: It is a cross-border shipment notification/documentation job for UK exporters, brokers and forwarding intermediaries, not domestic receiver record-keeping; it faces EU DIWASS compliance tooling and freight/customs software rather than the Defra-approved domestic provider list. It must be researched from scratch and may fail on whether the UK-side duty is felt and whether forwarders already perform it.

seeds.title: PRS registration and renewal help for self-managing individual landlords
seeds.observation: The PRS Database Regulations 2026 place a per-property registration, update (within 28 days) and annual renewal duty, with a fee payable before entry, on the person making a dwelling entry; the regime rolls out region by region from 15 December 2026 (West Midlands first) to all eligible England properties by 14 November 2027. The visible supply response targets letting agents and portfolios: a GBP29/month flat unlimited-properties PRS compliance platform with CSV import, and a major lettings platform publicly stating it is looking at how to support the process while integrating with agency CRMs that already hold compliance data. Nothing found targets the individual self-managing landlord who owns one or a few properties and must perform the same duty personally.
seeds.why_materially_different: The parent idea and the related seed prs-listing-precheck both sell into the professional channel (agents, portals, CRM vendors) and were contestable as a feature of lettings platforms and agent CRMs. This observation has a different buyer (individual self-managing landlords, consumer not B2B), a different mechanism (a consumer subscription that registers, updates and renews each property and tracks the numbers ahead of marketing) and a different competitive position (agent/platform tooling does not reach landlords who do not use an agent). It addresses the parent's recorded kill reason rather than restating it.
